name: Indian rebels of 1857
alt: Rebel government of Bahadur Shah Zafar

predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: Delhi, where the Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar was declared 'the Emperor of Hindustan'

predecessors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
predecessors.text: the places the rebels took from the Company in 1857

successors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
successors.text: the last rebel-held places, retaken by 20 June 1858

ledger.x: 10-11 May 1857: the sepoys of the Company's Meerut garrison mutiny on 10 May and reach Delhi the next day; Bahadur Shah Zafar is declared 'the Emperor of Hindustan' (the page dates the proclamation to mid-1857 and says he was coerced by the sepoys and his courtiers to sign it).
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 10 May 1857: the revolt begins; it was concentrated in the North-Western Provinces, Awadh, central India and parts of Bihar, while Bengal, Bombay and Madras stayed largely calm.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 11 May 1857: the rebels take Delhi: 'the rebels quickly reached Delhi' in the days after Meerut.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: June 1857: the Kanpur sepoys rebel under Nana Sahib and besiege the British entrenchment.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: Mid-July 1857: Kanpur 'was retaken by mid-July 1857' with reinforcements.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: September 1857: Delhi is retaken 'by the end of September', the siege (about 1 July-21 September) ending on 21 September.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 18 November 1857: Campbell's force evacuates the defended enclave at Lucknow, leaving the city to the rebels.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 21 March 1858: Campbell's second advance ends with the final fighting that drives the rebels out of Lucknow.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: March 1858: Hugh Rose's Central India Field Force besieges and captures Jhansi and the Rani flees; the page gives the siege in March and no capture day.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1 June 1858: after leaving Jhansi and Kalpi the Rani and the rebel forces capture Gwalior.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 17-20 June 1858: the Rani dies in the battle of Gwalior on 17 June and the Company forces recapture the city within three days.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 20 June 1858: the rebellion is contained with the rebels' defeat at Gwalior.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 20 June 1858: the rebel state ends at Gwalior.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

wars.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
wars.outcome: British victory (10 May 1857-20 June 1858); Delhi retaken in September 1857, Lucknow on 21 March 1858, Jhansi in March and Gwalior in June 1858; the Company dissolved under the Government of India Act of 1858.

wars.name: Siege of Delhi (1857)
wars.outcome: Delhi retaken by the end of September 1857 after a siege of about 1 July-21 September.

wars.name: Central India campaign (Jhansi and Gwalior)
wars.outcome: Hugh Rose's Central India Field Force takes Jhansi in March 1858; the rebels take Gwalior on 1 June and lose it again by 20 June 1858.

certainty.note: The rebels held cities and the districts around them in a shifting patchwork; the page maps no frontier.
